orgDesign.companyProfile: Amsterdam-based tax-technology company modeled on Reptune (formerly TP Tuned, founded 2015 by transfer pricing specialists Lennart van den Kommer and Allard Posthuma, later joined by David Zářecký, all with Big 4 and in-house experience) after Vortex Capital Partners became majority shareholder alongside management in the buyout announced on 5 August 2024. Reptune had 20 team members at the transaction; the company is modeled at about 40 people after the commercial scaling that Vortex backs (organisational infrastructure, sales development, go-to-market, international expansion). Its product Reptune.net automates Master Files, Local Files and Country-by-Country Reporting for 170+ countries for more than 150 multinationals with 5 to 500+ entities (TomTom, Stahl, Avnet, Ravago, Stanley Black & Decker among them), backed by ISO 27001-certified operations and a service model that runs from client-led On Demand to Reptune-led Full Service at fixed rates per Local File. Revenue is annual subscriptions by plan (Core, Advanced, Enterprise), add-ons (machine translation, CbCR and EU Public CbCR, SSO, R-AI Country Expert, custom templates, custom data models, custom development), fixed-rate documentation services and advisory hours. CEO and co-founder Lennart van den Kommer leads with CTO Giovanni Vajna de Pava and Head of Legal Alexandra Robins; Vortex managing partner Evert Jan de Groot sponsors the scaling thesis built on the proprietary software combined with deep transfer pricing knowledge.
orgDesign.operatingModel: With about 40 people the company is an expert-built organisation rather than a software vendor with a tax department: five small groups, each led by a working group lead, and eleven teams of 2-4 people in which software engineers sit next to transfer pricing specialists so that the rule-based data model, the OECD-aligned templates and the country rules are designed by people who have prepared documentation themselves. Stream-aligned teams own the annual lifecycle Model -> Scope -> Collect -> Generate -> Localise -> File -> Monitor -> Defend; a complicated-subsystem content team keeps regulations, deadlines, filing formats, languages and glossaries current for 170+ countries and turns each change into templates, validations and R-AI answers; two platform teams provide identity, divisions, audit trail, security and the ERP, operational transfer pricing, Excel, DocuSign and SSO integrations; an enabling AI team embeds R-AI, AI-assisted writing and machine translation into every workflow. The services arm operates the same platform: the full-service delivery team prepares documentation for outsourced clients in about a quarter of the time of a traditional adviser, and customer success and advisory runs onboarding in days, training, the included expert hours and consultation on value chain analysis, APAs, MAPs and controversy. Because specialists use the product every day, every pain point in delivery becomes a product change within the same small company, and clients can switch between On Demand, Collaborative and Full Service without rework. Every team is steward of the data assets its bricks create, so the intelligent transfer pricing data model and the country regulations knowledge base - the two strategic assets - stay coherent as the company scales.
